title: Orsen and the Passage
premise: Isandro Iversen, a railroad engineer haunted by a map of closed lines and the people he failed on them, trades his silence for a dying prospector's chart of a drowned mountain pass. Pursued by the railway company's enforcers who want the map destroyed, he joins forces with Maren, a boatwoman whose brother vanished in the pass, and together they navigate monsoon-flooded rivers to reach it before the waters seal it for another season. Isandro must choose between destroying the map to protect his own buried guilt and revealing the truth of the closed lines, which would save Maren's brother but ruin him. In the end he chooses truth over safety: the pass is opened, the dead are named, and Isandro—no longer running—stays to help rebuild what he once helped bury.
about_author: Tamsin Pemberton is a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years mapping river routes across monsoon country before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that remember what people try to forget.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept Moving
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He arrives in a river town with a forged work permit and a satchel of maps he should have burned years ago. A company inspector nearly catches him checking the old line ledgers. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of permanent flight, and the first hint that someone is following him.

chapters.title: A Trade at Dusk
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A feverish prospector named Oskar corners him in a dockside tavern and offers a hand-drawn map of the Vellmark Pass—closed since a collapse Isandro helped certify—for a promise: open it before the monsoon seals it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as opportunity; the past knocking loudly.

chapters.title: The Boatwoman
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She agrees to carry Isandro upriver only after seeing the map's mark near where her brother disappeared three years ago. She doesn't trust him, but she needs him. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged from two different griefs.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Two enforcers from the Northern Rail Company board their boat at a checkpoint, asking about a stolen map. Isandro lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: the cost of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: First Water
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The monsoon arrives early; they run the boat through rising rapids and discover the hull is cracked below the waterline. Isandro's engineering knowledge saves them, earning Maren's grudging respect. Emotional beat: competence as a fragile bridge between strangers.

chapters.title: What the Lines Closed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, told partly in memory. Flashback to the Vellmark collapse: the survey he falsified under orders, the eleven workers sealed inside, the promotion that bought his silence. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like something drowned coming up gasping.

chapters.title: The Leaking Hold
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Patching the boat overnight in a flooded boathouse, she catches Isandro studying her brother's name on an old manifest. Confrontation: she demands to know what he knows. He gives her half the truth. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared damage, poisoned by omission.

chapters.title: River Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The company men return with a warrant and a photograph of Oskar, now reported dead. Isandro realizes the prospector was murdered for the map—and that he is next. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Detour
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. To evade a river blockade they take a treacherous side channel through drowned farmland, where Maren reveals her family lost everything when the rail company rerouted the lines. Emotional beat: her anger reframing Isandro's complicity—he isn't just a witness.

chapters.title: Confession in the Rain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Trapped under a tarp during a storm, he finally tells Maren he signed the report that closed the pass with her brother inside it. She nearly abandons him on a mudbank. Emotional beat: truth offered too late, love and loyalty colliding head-on.

chapters.title: Cold Harbor
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She stays—not for him, but because only he can read the pass's old engineering drawings. They reach a derelict lock station and find evidence someone survived the collapse: scratched messages behind a bricked wall. Emotional beat: hope arriving in the shape of horror.

chapters.title: The Survivor's Mark
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The scratchings are dated months after the closure—someone lived. Isandro deciphers route notes suggesting survivors moved deeper into the pass toward an air shaft. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of a rescue twenty years too late, or not.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The company men ambush them at a fuel depot; Maren is wounded shielding the map case. They escape downriver but lose half their supplies. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by blood—the choice to keep going made physical.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Feverish from her wound, she makes Isandro promise that whatever they find, the names go public—even if it destroys him. He promises without knowing if he means it. Emotional beat: love against duty stated plainly, neither willing to blink.

chapters.title: The Last Lock
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They reach the final lock before the pass, jammed shut and rusted. Isandro must hand-crank mechanisms designed for a crew of twelve while the monsoon swells behind them. Emotional beat: endurance as penance; every turn of the wheel an apology.

chapters.title: Inside the Mountain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They enter the pass by lamplight: collapsed galleries, flooded tunnels, and a sealed chamber with fresh air moving through it. Someone has been keeping a fire alive here recently. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Living Record
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They find a journal kept by survivors' descendants—a hidden community that never left, living off seep water and smuggled supplies, including records naming every man sealed in. Her brother's name is there, marked 'went out.' Emotional beat: grief inverted—maybe no one to mourn, or worse.

chapters.title: Went Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The community's elder explains: some crawled out through the air shaft years ago; Maren's brother left for the coast and never wrote. But the company has tracked them here, and the enforcers arrive at the pass mouth with dynamite to seal it permanently—with everyone inside. Emotional beat: the trap closing on the innocent again.

chapters.title: The Choice of Maps
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cornered, he offers the enforcers a trade: the original map in exchange for the community's safety. It's a ruse—the map he surrenders is his own falsified survey, worthless and damning. Emotional beat: the liar using lying, finally, for something true.

chapters.title: Water Rising
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The climax: Isandro blows the old air-shaft plug to flood the enforcers' approach while Maren leads the community out through the lock passage as the monsoon peaks. Isandro is caught in the surge and swept into the dark. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest act left to him.

chapters.title: What the River Gave Back
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She drags Isandro from a backwater, barely alive, as the flood recedes. The enforcers are gone—drowned, fled, or discredited by the documents Isandro mailed upstream days earlier. Emotional beat: relief so fierce it feels like grief; the debt between them rewritten.

chapters.title: The Passage Open
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring: the pass is officially reopened, the eleven names carved in stone, the hidden community resettled. Maren's brother sends a letter from the coast. Isandro stays—first time in twenty years—to rebuild the line he broke. Emotional beat: stillness chosen freely; memory honored instead of outrun.
